message.reasoning_content:
Key suspicion: polynomial approximates exp(f*ln2) with fraction in [-0.5,0.5], but rounding via floor(x+0.5) — coefficients 0.69315 (truncated ln2!) and 0.24022, 0.0013391 (ln2^4/24?) — truncated coefficient precision likely yields error >1e-6 relative. Also scale via bitcast with exponent integer+127 — fine for range. Test numerically: run probe over all BF16 values in [-10,10] (~all bf16 grid) comparing to FP64 exp2.

Also floor(x+0.5) for x in [-0.5,0.5) gives integer 0 fine; but x=-10: integer=floor(-9.5)=-9, frac=-0.5. OK.

Also fp32 scale exact. Polynomial error: standard minimax with 0.693147 truncation to 0.69315 introduces ~3e-6? Actually 0.69315 vs 0.69314718 diff 2.8e-6 in the linear term; relative error ~2.8e-6*frac... at frac=0.5 that's ~1.4e-6*... exceeding 1e-6 tolerance. Likely bug. Test all bf16 values.
